plan_a_advantages: Incorporates strength and mobility training for injury prevention and efficient movement.
More frequent, shorter runs support better recovery and adaptation.
Includes cross-training for varied aerobic stimulus.
plan_b_advantages: Longer runs provide a solid foundation for endurance.
Focuses directly on aerobic development with moderate-intensity runs.
reasoning: For a goal of becoming a faster trail runner, Plan A is the superior choice. It incorporates a wider variety of training modalities – cross-training, strength work, and shorter, more frequent runs – which addresses the multifaceted demands of trail running. Plan B heavily emphasizes long, moderate-intensity runs, which, while important for endurance, don't directly target the speed component. Plan A’s inclusion of strength and mobility work is crucial for injury prevention and efficient movement on technical trails, something Plan B neglects. Furthermore, the more frequent, shorter runs in Plan A allow for better recovery and adaptation, crucial for consistent progress towards faster times.
